sections.title: Progress notice during analysis
sections.what: Draws the status panel with a stage heading, progress bar, counters and elapsed time, any error, the buttons that fit the job state, and a diagnostics block with the job identifier and cache state.
sections.why: Likely reason: a long analysis needs visible progress and a way out, and the job identifier helps when reporting a problem.
sections.watch_out: When the progress value is missing, the bar shows no clear amount, so check it again when adding new job states.

summary: Shows progress, elapsed time and cancel, resume or retry buttons while a schedule is being analysed.
purpose: Keeps the user informed during a long analysis and gives clear next steps when it stops or fails.
why: Likely reason: analysis can be slow or fail, so the user needs a visible state and a way out.
how: Shows nothing when there is no status or error. Otherwise it shows a stage name, a progress bar, counters, elapsed seconds, an error banner, action buttons, and a diagnostics block. A timer refreshes the elapsed time each second, only while work is running.
inputs: Current job state, progress status, busy flag, error text, cancelling flag, flags for resume and retry, and callbacks for cancel, resume and retry.
outputs: A notice on screen. Button clicks call the callbacks supplied by the parent.
risks: The progress value can be missing, which shows an unclear bar. Which buttons appear depends entirely on flags from the parent.
debug: If the wrong button shows, check canResume and canRetry in the parent. If counts look wrong, check the job state fields and the status stage.
